name: ND at-large
label: Safe R

key_factors: Fedorchak's roughly $2.1M-to-$341K fundraising edge and $1.1M cash advantage
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 97%
No public polls or outside spending signal a competitive race
model.rationale: Every available signal points the same way: the district's deep Republican lean, Fedorchak's roughly six-to-one fundraising advantage as the incumbent, and prediction markets pricing a Republican win around 97%, with no polling suggesting Hammer is competitive.
model.watch: A late influx of Democratic outside spending or a poll showing Hammer within single digits would be the first visible sign of a real contest, though neither currently exists.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
North Dakota's at-large House seat sits in territory that leans about eighteen points toward Republicans, and incumbent Julie Fedorchak enters the general election with the advantages typical of defending a safe seat. She has raised roughly $2.1 million and holds about $1.1 million in cash, while Democratic nominee Trygve Hammer has raised about $341,000 with roughly $75,000 on hand. Two independent candidates are on the ballot but show no measurable fundraising.

No public general-election polling is available, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. Prediction markets put Hammer's chances at roughly three percent. The fundraising gap, the district's partisan lean, and the absence of any visible Democratic outside spending all point to a comfortable Republican win, with the open question being the size of Fedorchak's margin rather than the outcome.
